answer: Total inventory value is SAR 20,245,522.22 across all six stock statuses, all at plant GM01. By status: unrestricted 17,204,144.82; quality inspection 2,264,900.52; returns 302,426.83; blocked 283,910.56; in transit 113,382.56; restricted 76,756.92. Only unrestricted and quality inspection have stored values (together SAR 19,469,045.34); the other four are quantity times unit price.
how_calculated: Used v_stock (one row per storage location, material and status), excluded source_row 5064, and summed the stored source_value where present, otherwise quantity * valuation_price. Check: the same total from sap_mb52 joined to sap_material_master on material and plant gave 20245522.21732. Pure price times quantity on every row gave 20245485.67772, a difference of 36.54 that comes from 5 rows whose stored value differs from price times quantity.
assumptions: Inventory value means all stock statuses, including blocked, returns, restricted and in transit. If returns are not valued, the total is SAR 19,943,095.38. If only stored values count, it is SAR 19,469,045.34. Source row 5064 is an exact duplicate of row 9 (material 004100007, S011, 20 EA, SAR 882.20) and is removed; with it the total is SAR 20,246,404.42. The sap_mb52_totals footer is not added, and its figures include the duplicate. unit_price (price / price_unit) is the per-unit price, so items priced per 100 are not overstated. Understated: 44 stock rows have no price or a zero price and count as zero, covering 41 unrestricted, 2 quality inspection and 1 blocked row. All values are SAR. Stock exists only for GM01 in this data; GM02 and GM03 have no stock rows.
sql: with s as (select * from v_stock where source_row<>5064) select stock_status, sum(coalesce(source_value, quantity*valuation_price)) val from s group by rollup(stock_status) order by 1

answer: Unrestricted stock is worth SAR 17,204,144.82, all at plant GM01.

Quantity * price on v_stock gave 17204990.48016 before removing the duplicate, which is 36.54 below the stored 17205027.02.
assumptions: Source row 5064 is an exact duplicate of row 9 and is removed (SAR 882.20). With it, the figure is SAR 17,205,027.02, which matches the sap_mb52_totals footer, so the footer includes the duplicate. Stored values are used as they stand. 41 unrestricted rows have no price or a zero price and are valued at zero, so the figure is understated: 3,502 EA, 3,444.003 KG, 1,654.94 L, 831.745 M, 634 PC and 1,621 ROL. sql: with d as (select distinct plant,storage_location,material,base_uom,unrestricted,quality_inspection,value_quality_inspection,transit_transfer,restricted_use,blocked,returns,value_unrestricted from sap_mb52) select sum(value_unrestricted) from d

answer: Blocked stock is 1,537 EA, 148.151 KG, 881.282 M and 481 PC, across 13 rows at plant GM01. There is no blocked stock in L, ROL or SET. Valued at unit price, this is about SAR 283,910.56.
how_calculated: Summed blocked by base_uom in sap_mb52, excluding the duplicate source row. Checks: the sap_mb52_totals footer shows the same quantity for each unit, and v_stock with status blocked has 13 rows with the same overall quantity. Value is blocked * unit_price from sap_material_master joined on material and plant, and matches quantity * valuation_price in v_stock (283910.56464).
assumptions: How much is read as quantity, reported per unit because units must not be added; the SAR value is also given. Blocked has no stored value, so the value is calculated from the price. Material 004101918 (183 PC blocked) has a zero price, so the SAR value is understated.
sql: select base_uom, sum(blocked) qty, count(*) filter (where blocked>0) n from sap_mb52 where source_row<>5064 group by 1 order by 1

answer: There are 15 distinct A-class materials, in 20 material and plant records (GM01 15, GM02 1, GM03 4).
how_calculated: Counted distinct material in sap_material_master where abc_indicator = 'A'. Check: grouping by plant gave 15, 1 and 4 records, 20 in total, and no material has different ABC classes across plants.

sql: select count(*) rec, count(distinct material) mats from sap_material_master where abc_indicator='A'

answer: 89 material master records are priced per 100 units, covering 73 distinct materials.
how_calculated: Counted rows in sap_material_master where price_unit = 100. Check: grouping by price_unit gave 1,769 records at 1, 1 at 3 and 89 at 100, which adds to 1,859 total. unit_price equals price / price_unit on all priced records.
assumptions: Records means material and plant rows, as the question asks, so a material at several plants counts once per plant. price_unit means the number of units the price covers, confirmed by unit_price = price / price_unit and by stored stock values matching that per-unit price.
sql: select count(*) rec, count(distinct material) mats from sap_material_master where price_unit=100

answer: Material 004108785 (PIGMENT 949) has the highest unrestricted stock value: SAR 1,756,182.64, from 316 EA across 2 storage locations at GM01.
how_calculated: Summed value_unrestricted by material in sap_mb52 and took the largest. Check: 316 EA at the master unit price of SAR 5,557.54 agrees with the stored value. Next is 004101099 (PUMP UNIT 548) at SAR 1,190,852.24.
assumptions: Single material means one material number summed across its storage locations, not one location row. Grouping is by material number, because some descriptions are shared by two materials. Unpriced stock counts as zero, so an unpriced material could not rank here. The duplicate row concerns a different material, so it has no effect.
sql: select material, max(material_description) d, sum(value_unrestricted) v, sum(unrestricted) u, max(base_uom) uom from sap_mb52 group by 1 order by v desc limit 5
